Alabama's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP state option;
PolicyEngine models gross screen x1.3 FPL, x2.0 for elderly/disabled
households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in
the composed us-al/snap/fy-2026 program, which applies only the standard
federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
persisted output surface: the household passes axiom's gross test and
fails only the net-income test, which the state's BBCE waives. Axiom-
side modeling boundary, tracked for encoding in rulespec-us#1098.

Reverified on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The exact-household signature and explicit K-12 counterfactual reproduce the mechanism: PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7). The sole minor is a valid household under 273.1(a)(1), but wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so Axiom correctly fails the income gate and returns zero benefit. The true-January regeneration preserves the same four paired benefit/eligibility selectors. In case-id order, PolicyEngine benefits moved from 296.8949788411458, 299.66998291015625, 150.64496866861978, and 299.66998291015625 to 294.70001220703125, 298.0, 148.59999084472656, and 298.0; Axiom remains ineligible with zero benefit for all four, so the amount movement does not change the evidenced classification.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 785.0 versus January PolicyEngine 744.5); the January PolicyEngine value is reproduced by the direct requested-month simulation with the imputed SSI input forced to zero (744.5), so the committed value carries endogenous TANF but not SSI. Forcing the aggregate and state TANF inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 785.0; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.0, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The comparison bridge zeroes TANF on the Axiom input surface while PolicyEngine computes state TANF endogenously and counts it as SNAP unearned income (axiom-oracles#397 counterfactual class). Replay classifier record: class=tanf_reanchored_no_ssi.

Self-employment loss pass-through: the projection's flat 0.6 self-employment netting (axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml) passes Enhanced CPS self-employment losses through as negative Axiom earned income (sample ecps-73185: persisted snap_gross_monthly_earned_income -296073.92), while PolicyEngine floors SNAP self-employment income at zero (snap_self_employment_income_after_expense_deduction takes max(., 0)). Axiom's income tests pass on the loss-netted surface and it awards a benefit while PolicyEngine remains ineligible or lower. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values, and every selected row carries a negative Axiom earned-income input while the January PolicyEngine earned income is floored at or above zero (1 cases / 2 rows). A dedicated tracking issue for the self-employment-loss netting in the Populace bridge still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-cross-program-input policy problem (same linkage as the fl-snap-ecps se-loss-netting class).

The comparison's PolicyEngine eligibility boolean comes from the batch output dataset's calendar-2026 aggregation, which reports eligible although the direct requested-month (2026-01) simulation is ineligible for January: the household fails the January income eligibility tests under the FY-2026 parameters while other 2026 months pass (income-limit uprating across the October fiscal-year boundary), and Axiom evaluates 2026-01 only. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the annual-aggregated True while the direct January simulation returns False on every selected row (1 rows; sample ecps-37198 January gross-income-to-poverty ratio 1.3059). The January benefit is zero on both engines, so only the eligibility boolean diverges — a harness period-aggregation artifact, not an engine defect.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 0 versus January PolicyEngine 0). Forcing the imputed medical-expense inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 0; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.0, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. Axiom receives zero medical-expense input while PolicyEngine imputes allowable medical expenses for the elderly/disabled member, feeding an excess medical deduction the bridge never projects to Axiom. The same intervention sets January PolicyEngine eligibility to False, matching Axiom's persisted verdict.

Reverified per-row on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3 via exact-household requested-month replay: for every selected row January PolicyEngine grants broad-based categorical eligibility (meets_snap_categorical_eligibility=True) while a standard federal income test fails, and pays the resulting benefit (one/two-person minimums where net income leaves no normal allotment). The composed program applies only the standard federal tests, so Axiom is ineligible with zero benefit. Axiom-side modeling boundary. Per-row flags: ecps-36581: categorical=True, net_test=False, gross_test=True, January PE 23.84.
